Definition: of uncertain affinity; to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away:--fade away.
BiblicalUsage: maraínō is to fade away, like a flower scorched by the sun, and it occurs once, in James 1:11. There the sun rises with burning heat and withers the grass, and the flower falls, and the grace of its fashion perishes, and so shall the rich man fade away in his ways. The word is glory wilting in the heat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe maraínō shows me that the rich man's glory withers like a flower in the heat, and I will not build my life on what fades.
